title: US court jails Nikhil Gupta for over 19 years over plot to kill Pannun
dek: A New York judge sentenced the Indian national to 235 months for a murder-for-hire plot that US prosecutors say was directed by an Indian government employee. India denies any role.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A federal judge in New York on Friday sentenced Nikhil Gupta, an Indian national, to 235 months in prison, just over 19 and a half years, for his part in a foiled plot to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, a Sikh separatist leader whom India designates a terrorist. The sentence, handed down by US District Judge Victor Marrero in Manhattan late on Friday India time, is the first in a case in which US prosecutors say the killing was directed by an Indian government employee.

Gupta, 55, had pleaded guilty in February to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. He is expected to be deported to India after serving his term, according to reports. India has denied any involvement in the plot and says such an act would be against government policy.

## What happened in court

Prosecutors had asked for about 24 years in prison; Gupta's lawyers asked for 12, according to reports. The judge settled on 235 months, the bottom of the range that prosecutors had calculated under the US sentencing guidelines, followed by three years of supervised release, according to the Justice Department.

Announcing the sentence, the US Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, said the case showed the government's commitment to prosecuting plots to commit violence on American soil, "regardless of where they were located", according to the department's release as reported.

In court, prosecutor Ashley Nicolas said: "This case cuts to the very core of American values. We don't condone the use of violence to silence voices in this country, ever," according to reports.

Gupta addressed the court before he was sentenced. He said he regretted departing from the non-violent example of Mahatma Gandhi, and added: "I'm sorry to Mr Pannun, I'm sorry to the communities I hurt, I'm sorry to my own family," according to reports.

## The case against him

According to the US Justice Department, a man it identifies as Vikash Yadav, who it says worked in India's Cabinet Secretariat, the office that houses the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), recruited Gupta in May 2023 to arrange the killing of Mr Pannun in New York.

Prosecutors say Gupta looked for a contract killer through a contact who was in fact a confidential source for the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The source introduced him to an undercover DEA officer posing as a hitman. Mr Yadav agreed to pay $100,000 for the killing, and an associate handed over $15,000 in cash as an advance on 9 June 2023, according to the department.

Prosecutors say Mr Yadav passed Gupta Mr Pannun's New York address and details of his daily routine, which Gupta forwarded to the undercover officer with surveillance photographs. Gupta asked that the killing not take place around Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit to the United States, which began on 20 June 2023, according to prosecutors.

After Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a Sikh separatist leader, was shot dead outside a gurdwara in British Columbia, Canada, on 18 June 2023, Gupta told the undercover officer that Mr Nijjar had also been a target and that there was no longer any need to wait, the prosecution says.

Gupta was arrested in Prague on 30 June 2023 at the request of the United States and extradited in June 2024. He has been in custody in Brooklyn since.

## Background

Mr Yadav is charged in the same case but is not in US custody, and any trial would depend on extradition from India. India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has said he is no longer a government employee. India set up a high-level inquiry committee after Washington first raised the allegations in 2023.

Mr Pannun, a US and Canadian citizen, is the founder and legal counsel of Sikhs for Justice, which campaigns for a separate Sikh state. India banned the group in 2019 and has designated him a terrorist; he is wanted in India on terrorism charges.

The criminal case runs alongside a separate civil lawsuit that Mr Pannun filed in New York in September 2024 against the Government of India, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, former RAW chief Samant Goel, Gupta, Mr Yadav and others. On Friday, before the sentencing, the MEA rejected the New York court's latest attempt to deliver summonses in that case through courts in Delhi. "We reject such baseless lawsuits," the ministry's spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, said, according to reports.

In Canada, four Indian nationals are awaiting trial over Mr Nijjar's killing, according to reports. India denies any role in it.

## What they are saying

Mr Pannun attended the hearing. He called Gupta "just a foot soldier" and said the Modi government wanted him dead because he campaigns openly, according to reports. He described the sentence as "the first step" and said those who directed and paid for the plot should also be held to account.

The Government of India had not commented publicly on the sentence by Saturday evening. Its position, set out by the MEA since 2023, is that it does not support such acts, that Mr Yadav is no longer in its employment, and that the allegations in the civil case are "fabricated and malicious".

## Why it matters for India

The sentence lands in the middle of a busy stretch for India's relations with the United States and Canada. Mr Modi met President Donald Trump at the Quad summit in Manila earlier this month, and the two countries are negotiating a trade agreement. Mr Modi is also due to visit Canada on 11 and 12 December and is expected to meet Prime Minister Mark Carney, according to reports; Mr Pannun has urged Ottawa to put "accountability before trade".

Day-to-day security cooperation has continued. On Saturday, Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated India's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the DEA on a joint operation, "Operation Monsoon Thunder", against a network that the NCB said supplied psychotropic and opioid tablets to buyers in the United States. Six people were arrested, and about 3,000 parcels holding nearly 5 lakh tablets were identified, according to the NCB. The US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, praised the partnership.

## What happens next

Gupta can appeal against the sentence; no appeal had been reported by Saturday. The charges against Mr Yadav remain pending in New York, and the civil suit against Mr Doval and others is still before a different judge in the same court. In Canada, the trial of the four men accused over Mr Nijjar's killing has not yet concluded.

## Timeline

- May 2023: Gupta recruited, according to US prosecutors
- 9 June 2023: $15,000 advance handed over, prosecutors say
- 18 June 2023: Hardeep Singh Nijjar killed in British Columbia
- 30 June 2023: Gupta arrested in Prague
- June 2024: Gupta extradited to the United States
- September 2024: Pannun files civil suit in New York
- February 2026: Gupta pleads guilty
- 20 November 2026: Gupta sentenced to 235 months
